Hyderabad is rationing piped water to once every three days and fining pubs up to Rs 20,000 for washing floors with drinking water. But videos of water gushing onto streets in two localities have left residents asking who will answer for those leaks.  
  
In one video, from Maula Ali, Manjeera water is seen running down a road. In the other, from SR Nagar, water spills from a pump outside JJ Hospital.  
  
Both clips spread on social media, with users asking who was responsible for letting water go to waste in the middle of a crisis.  
  
“Restaurants and pubs were asked to pay a Rs 20,000 fine for wasting water. Who should be penalised for this pump, which is leaking water?” asked Mohammed Ilyas, who posted the SR Nagar video on Instagram.  
  
Fines for some:  
The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) has been fining people, restaurants and pubs between Rs 5,000 and Rs 20,000 for wasting water while cleaning their premises. One city pub was recently fined Rs 20,000.  
  
From November 1, water tankers caught spilling drinking water on the way will also be fined Rs 5,000. HMWSSB Managing Director K Ashok Reddy issued the order on October 24 after the board found tankers being overfilled and water splashing onto roads.  
  
Tankers with leaks, missing lids or loose covers will not be filled until they are repaired.  
  
The Maula Ali leak has struck a nerve because the Manjeera is one of the sources under the most strain. The board expects a shortfall of about 100 million gallons a day (MGD) from Singur and Manjeera between January and August.

# HMWSSB warns residents against water wastage, threatens to disconnect services

Published - September 21, 2026 07:45 pm IST - HYDERABAD

The Hindu Bureau

SEE ALL
Remove

The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) has issued serious warning against water wastage, after imposing penalties in five such instances on Monday. Second time offenders will attract disconnection of water supply, it warned.

All the five penalised were residents of Jubilee Hills, and found to have been wasting water, during inspections conducted by the Board officials.

The inspections will be intensified in the coming days, and second time offenders will be penalised through disconnection of water supply, the note warned.

Using drinking water to wash floor and vehicles, leaving the tap open, and not shutting down the pump set even after overhead tank overflows are some of the instances of water wastage, as shared by the Board.

Despite awareness campaigns and warnings, the users are still found resorting to the same practices, calling for penalties. The penalties which had started with just ₹1000 per instance, have over the time risen to ₹5,000, then ₹10,000 and now ₹20,000. Still the violations continue to persist. the note said.

Leakages in the water supply network too will be plugged by officials within 24 hours of identification, and in case of dereliction of duties, action will be taken against officials and staff too. The water board’s drinking water pipeline extends to 15,000 kilometres in the city, to plug leakages in which, a special action plan is being be taken up. The officials have been directed to identify locations with frequent leakages and provide permanent solutions.

# Hyderabad: Drinking water samples being tested across city

#### In Short

The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) has obtained 10,400 samples of drinking water and conducted water quality tests in the last 24 hours

The Hans India

Created On:  19 Oct 2020 1:19 AM ISTComment

##### Share :

X

Telangana govt. waives off 13 months water bill for consumers

Font size

**Hyderabad**: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) has obtained 10,400 samples of drinking water and conducted water quality tests in the last 24 hours. This is four times greater than the collected samples during working days.

In view of the heavy rains, KT Rama Rao, Minister of Municipal Administration and Urban Development, directed HMWSSB officials to increase the collection of water samples and to ensure that no pollution of drinking water occurs.

HMWSSB is taking up the work at a cost of Rs.1.20 crore, following the Minister's orders to speed up the reconstruction and repair of damaged water and sewer lines. Drinking water is given in cans and water sachets are also distributed in all areas impacted by rain.

Households are called upon to clear and sanitise all the water contained in sumps and tanks with bleaching powder. In addition, chlorine tabs were also provided to be combined as a precautionary measure in drinking water to prevent any water-borne diseases.

HMWSSB MD M Dana Kishore said 700 additional staff were deployed during a teleconference with officials to tackle sewer choking at the customer's premises and answer other complaints.

Officials were given orders to repair overflowing manholes on roads and settlements on a priority basis. Officials were directed to ensure that masks, gloves and helmets and other protective equipment were worn by all sanitary staff when taking up work.

HMWSSB has produced proposals for cleaning and minor repairs to tanks at a cost of Rs.50 lakh. Apart from this, Rs. 5 lakh was approved by each General Manager to clean up reservoirs within the limits of the Outer Ring Road.

# Metro Board rolls out spl steps to prevent water contamination

#### In Short

The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) is taking special measures to prevent contamination of drinking water due to rains.

The Hans India

Created On:  4 Sept 2024 7:03 AM ISTComment

##### Share :

X

Font size

**Hyderabad:** The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) is taking special measures to prevent contamination of drinking water due to rains. A special committee, comprising high-level officials, has been formed to monitor water logging points, overflow, and pollution in the city and along the Outer Ring Road (ORR).

HMWSSB Managing Director Ashok Reddy inspected various localities on Tuesday and stated that precautions are being taken to ensure adequate chlorine levels in the drinking water supplied by the Water Board through the special committee.

To address this, the department has implemented a three-step chlorination process. In the first phase, chlorination occurs at the Water Treatment Plants (WTP). In the second phase, it is carried out at the Main Balancing Reservoirs (MBR). Finally, booster chlorination is done at the service reservoirs. Precautions are being taken to ensure that the water supplied contains exactly 0.5 ppm of chlorine.

The Water Board is exercising heightened caution in supplying water to slums, flood-affected areas, and low-lying regions of the city, taking measures to prevent the distribution of contaminated water in these areas. To support this, 8.80 lakh chlorine tablets have been distributed in flood-affected zones, slums, and low-lying areas.

Additionally, residents are being educated on how to purify water using these chlorine tablets.

Water Board officials advise the public not to open manhole lids under any circumstances. If a manhole cover is broken or left open, residents should contact customer care at 155313 for issues related to contaminated water and other concerns.

This is the Official website of Hyderabad Metropolitan Water supply and Sewerage Board, Department of MA&UD, Ministry of Municipal Administration, Government of Telangana, designed, developed, and hosted by IT WING of HMWSSB.

The site has been developed to provide information to the general public. An attempt has been made through this site to provide reliable, comprehensive, accurate information about Water Supply and Sewerage System of HMWSSB under jurisdiction HMWSSB.

The content in this site is the result of a collaborative effort of various Groups and Divisions of the Department. It is our endeavour to continue the enhancement and enrichment of this site in terms of content coverage, design, and technology on a regular basis.

Content Contribution, Moderation & Approval Policy (CMAP)

Content needs to be contributed by the authorized Content Manager from various wings of HMWSSB in a consistent fashion to maintain uniformity and bring in standardization along with associated metadata and keywords.

The content on the portal goes through the entire lifecycle process, which consists of:

Once the content is contributed, it needs to be approved and moderated prior to being published on the Website. The moderation could be multilevel and is role-based. If the content is rejected at any level, it is reverted back to the originator of the content for modification.

Different Content Element is categorized as:

(Approver and the moderator for each of the content element)

| SECTIONS | ROLES |
| --- | --- |
| CONTRIBUTOR | MODERATOR | APPROVER |
| Home Page & Common Section e.g, FAQs, Help etc | General Manager (IT) | General Manager (IT) | Director (Technical) |
| Who's Who, Organization Chart, Circulars/Notifications, Profile | General Manager (P&A) | General Manager (P&A) | General Manager (IT) |
| Citizen Charter | General Manager (P&A) | General Manager (P&A) | General Manager (IT) |
| Statues | General Manager (P&A) | General Manager (P&A) | Director (P&A) |
| O&M Wing | DCE, Director (Operations) | DCE, Director (Operations) | Director (Operations) |
| Projects | DCE, Director (Projects) | DCE, Director (Projects) | Director (Projects) |
| News/Events, Awards etc | Public Relation Officer | Public Relation Officer | General Manager (IT) |
| Prospective Customer Services | General Manager (E), SWC Wing | General Manager (E), SWC Wing | General Manager (IT) |
| RTI | General Manager (P&A) | General Manager (P&A) | General Manager (IT) |
| Source and Storage | CGM (E)/Transmission Circle | CGM (E)/Transmission Circle | Director (Technical) |
| Tenders | Concerned Head of the Department | Concerned Head of the Department | General Manager (IT) |

HMWSSB website is an important tool for disseminating the information to the masses being served by the organization. It is therefore required to keep the content on the Website current and up-to-date and hence there is a need for the Content Review Policy. Since the scope of the content is huge, different Review Policies are defined for the diverse content elements.

The Review Policy is based on different type of content elements, its validity and relevance as well as the archival policy. The matrix below gives the Content Review Policy:

The entire website content would be reviewed for syntax check once a fortnightly by the HMWSSB Website

| Section | Review Periodicity |
| --- | --- |
| Home Page | Daily |
| News Page | Daily |
| Who's Who list | As and When required |
| Newsletter, Circulars, Notifications etc | As and when required |
| Act, Rules | As and When required |

The Guidelines for Indian Government Websites (GIGW) stipulate that expired contents must not be presented or flashed on the website. Therefore, as per the content archival policy adopted by this department, contents will be deleted from the site after its expiry date. Important data will be shifted to the archives page. Therefore, the content contributors should revalidate/modify the content periodically to ensure that expired data is not present/flashed in the site. Wherever contents are no longer needed to be displayed, suitable advice may be sent to the web information manager for their archival/deletion.

Each of the content components is accompanied by meta data, source and validity date. For some of the components the validity date may not be known i.e., the content is stated to be perpetual. Under this scenario, the validity date should be Ten years.

For few of the components like announcements, tenders, only the live content whose validity date is after the current date is shown on the Website. For other components like documents, schemes, services, forms, websites and contact directory there is a need for timely review of the same as per the Content Review Policy.

Entry/Exit Policy and Archival Policy for the content elements on the HMWSSB website will be as per the following table:

Table- (Content Archival Policy)

| S.No. | Content Element | Entry Policy | Exit Policy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | About Department | Whenever Department is realigned/ changes its work distribution. | Perpetual (10 years) |
| 2 | Programme/Schemes | Discontinuation of Programme/Schemes for Central/State Sector. | Five (05) years |
| 3 | Policies | Discontinuation by Government – Central/State | Perpetual (10 years) |
| 4 | Acts/Rules | Issued through gazette/ Passed by Government | Perpetual (10 years) |
| 5 | Circulars/ Notifications | Overruling Office Memorandum or Notification issued. | Five (05) years since date of discontinuation. |
| 6 | Documents/Publications/Reports | Completion of its validity period. | Perpetual (10 years) since date of entry into archival. |
| 7 | Directories | Not required | Not Applicable |

Hyderabad Water Board Dismisses Rumours of Water Shortage

Hyderabad: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) has dismissed rumours claiming that reservoirs supplying water to Hyderabad would run dry by the end of November due to the El Niño effect.

A fake message circulating on social media claims that water supply across the city could be severely restricted or completely stopped due to falling reservoir levels. The Water Board clarified that these claims are false and that no such official message has been issued.

HMWSSB urged residents not to believe or forward unverified messages circulated in the name of Jalmandali. The Board also appealed to the public to use water responsibly and avoid wastage.
